resale_co.name: Residential Transfer of Ownership Certificate (Certificate of Continued Occupancy, CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Emerson Building Department, with the Fire Prevention Bureau doing the smoke/CO part
resale_co.lead_time: The Borough recommends applying 3 to 4 weeks before the closing date
requirements: Combined application for the transfer of ownership certificate and the smoke alarm / carbon monoxide alarm / fire extinguisher inspection (one form, two checks)
Homeowner checklist used at the CCO inspection: smoke alarms on each level and within 10 feet of bedrooms, CO alarms near bedrooms, fire extinguisher mounted in the kitchen (form still lists it)
In-ground oil tanks must have certification
Sump pump must drain to the exterior, not into the waste line
Monitored fire alarms need a certification from the monitoring company and police registration
Garage door openers on a dedicated outlet; keyless deadbolt on the inside of the front door; working GFI outlets in the kitchen; dryer vented outside
Bedroom windows must operate and be the correct size for egress; house number visible from the street; hydrant on the property kept visible
Pool barrier in good repair with self-closing, self-latching gates; property neat and clean; secure flue connections at boiler, furnace and water heater

fees.quote: CCO FEE: $105 CHECK MADE OUT TO BOROUGH OF EMERSON.

fees.quote: fee of $45.00 is required to be paid.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Borough's Application for Residential Transfer of Ownership Certificate (on the Forms page), give the closing date, seller, buyer, block and lot and a contact, and pay two checks: the CCO fee to the Borough of Emerson and the smoke/CO fee to the Fire Prevention Bureau. Payments and paperwork can be left in the drop box by the Building Department window on the Municipal Place side of Borough Hall. Questions go to the Building Department at 201-262-6086 ext. 1214 or buildingadmin@emersonnj.gov.

evidence.quote: CCO FEE: $105 CHECK MADE OUT TO BOROUGH OF EMERSON.
Drain directly to the exterior. NOT into Waste Line.
Certificate of continued occupancy: UCC, applicant requested:
A certificate of occupancy shall be required for both initial and continued occupancy, and use of the building or land to which it applies, as certified.

resale_co.notes: The Borough's Residential Transfer of Ownership Certificate form (Building Department and Fire Prevention Bureau, per Ordinance No. 1618-20) is a combined CCO and smoke/CO application, and its homeowner checklist is titled for Certificate of Continued Occupancy inspections. I could not find the exact code section that requires the CCO on a resale; Chapter 128 (Certificates of Occupancy, Section 128-1G) says a CO is required for both initial and continued occupancy. Fees do not line up across sources: the form says the CCO fee is $105, the construction fee schedule (Section 132-3A(1)(m)) lists $125 per subcode for an applicant-requested certificate of continued occupancy, and Section 128-1D lists $150 for a residential certificate of occupancy; confirm the current amount with the office. Code text was read through the ecode360 print view. The form lists the address as 1 Municipal Place; the website contact block lists 146 Linwood Avenue. Rental programs (Residential Certification of Rental Occupancy form, landlord registration, lead-based paint inspection) are not resale requirements.

requirements: Smoke alarms on every level (basement, first floor, second floor), excluding crawl spaces and unfinished attics, and outside each separate sleeping area within 10 feet of bedrooms
All battery-operated smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units
Carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of bedroom areas in the hallway, permanently mounted or plug-in

Portable fire extinguisher, at least 2A:10B:C and no more than 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen in the exit path, top no more than 5 feet above the floor, serviced and tagged by a state-certified contractor in the past 12 months or with a recent purchase receipt (form still lists it)

authorities.name: Emerson Fire Prevention Bureau
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how far ahead the inspection is scheduled from when the paperwork is submitted: 10 days or more for the lowest fee. The Borough recommends submitting 3 to 4 weeks before closing.

fees.label: Smoke and CO alarm inspection scheduled 10 days or more from paperwork submittal
fees.quote: $45 if inspection is scheduled 10 days or more from date of paperwork submittal.

fees.label: Smoke and CO alarm inspection scheduled more than 4 but less than 10 days from paperwork submittal (Code Section 150-7F)
fees.quote: $90 if inspection is scheduled more than four days but less than 10 days from date of paperwork submittal.

fees.label: Smoke and CO alarm inspection scheduled 4 days or less from paperwork submittal
fees.quote: $161 if inspection is scheduled four days or less from date of paperwork submittal.

fees.label: Each additional inspection after a failed inspection
fees.quote: Any failed inspections will require a $45 fee for each additional inspection.

fees.label: Smoke/CO fee as printed on the transfer form, less than 10 days (form amount)
fees.quote: $95 IF LESS THAN 10 DAYS AND $161 IF LESS THAT 4 DAYS.

authorities.how_to_apply: Use the same Residential Transfer of Ownership Certificate form as the CCO. Mark the smoke and CO alarm types (hardwired, battery or low voltage) and pay the smoke/CO fee by check made out to the Fire Prevention Bureau. Fire Prevention Bureau office hours are Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 8:30 AM to 3:00 PM.

fire_cert.notes: The Borough code (Section 150-7F, amended 7-25-2023 by Ord. No. 1675-23, read through the ecode360 print view) sets $45 (10 days or more), $90 (more than 4 but less than 10 days) and $161 (4 days or less), plus $45 per reinspection. The transfer form instead prints $95 for less than 10 days; the code amount is likely current but confirm. The form and checklist still list a portable fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed from the sale certificate in February 2025. The NJ DCA fire directory lists the Fire Official as Anthony J Sottile with an emersonnj.org email; the Borough's own page now uses fireofficial@emersonnj.gov and 201-927-3262 (the main Borough number is 201-262-6086).

other_items.label: Oil tank certification
other_items.detail: The CCO homeowner checklist says in-ground oil tanks must have certification.

other_items.label: Sump pump discharge
other_items.detail: The CCO checklist requires the sump pump to drain to the exterior, not into the waste (sewer) line.

other_items.label: Monitored fire alarm certification
other_items.detail: If the home has a monitored fire alarm, a certification from the monitoring company that it works is needed, and the system must be registered with the Police.
